choices: No one: it is recorded only
qs.explain: Point-of-care ultrasound is focused, done at the bedside and interpreted by the provider performing it, in real time. The comprehensive study is performed by a sonographer and read by a radiologist, taking hours to days.

qs.q: Which probe frequency gives better resolution but less depth?
qs.explain: Higher frequency: better resolution, less depth. Lower frequency: better depth, less resolution. Gain is brightness and depth is how far you are zoomed in.

qs.q: Vertical bright lines from the pleura in a dyspneic patient point to what?
qs.explain: B lines are vertical hyperechoic lines from an air-water interface, seen with pulmonary edema. Horizontal A lines are the normal lung.

qs.q: Which cardiac window is best for a pericardial effusion?
qs.explain: The subxiphoid view, using the liver as a window, is best for pericardial effusion since most effusions are inferior. The apical four chamber view is for right ventricular strain.

qs.q: A vein that will not compress under the probe means what?
qs.explain: Thrombus will not be compressible: the major diagnostic feature of a deep vein thrombosis. Normal veins are completely compressible; arteries are pulsatile with minimal compressibility.
